thread_title: S. flava var. cuprea clone #3 Brunswick Co, NC
breadcrumb: S. flava var. cuprea clone #3 Brunswick Co, NC

posts.body_html:
To preface the description of this clone, I have another clone in the collection that was almost completely lost to rot this past winter, but a growth point was salvaged. Being so distraught, I almost went into depression: I mean, look at this thing!




The reason this clone is very significant is because of that red throat: I'm told that in the Carolinas, the cut throat trait isn't very common. I've never been to the Carolinas, so I can't confirm or deny this statement, maybe someone with experience can chime in?


Anyways, back on topic: the good news is, my fragile emotions quickly healed once the remaining side shoot rooted, but the sprits were greatly lifted after seeing another clone in the collection that is just like it! Well, it still looks subtly different, but it has that red throat trait going on.

Here's S. flava var. cuprea clone#3 Brunswick Co, NC, pics taken 5/28/21:




Just noticed the yellowish interior in the mouth, pretty cool:

posts.body_html: Pure cutthroats (aka rugelii) aren't generally found any more north outside of the SC Sandhills. There are a few rugelii mixed in there with maxima and var flava, but it's definitely the outlier in coloration. Most SC/NC cupreas that i've seen don't have anywhere near the amount of throat blotch as this clone, with the exception of MKF216 (Greenswamp) and a few others where the color completely fills the throat and underside of the lid.
